items_missed: Set Agenda: no move-date availability check, no agenda statement (what we'll cover + rough time), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
Probe: no zip code captured for origin or destination; didn't ask about special considerations, packing needs, box count, additional stops, or moving stressors.

Pricing: never itemized what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, tools); no disassembly/reassembly mention; skipped No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the no-hidden-fees pitch entirely.
Clock: never explained when the clock starts, the 15-minute prorated increments, or did a sense-check ('does that make sense?').

Estimate: let the customer's math ($200 + $200 = $400) stand uncorrected even though the stated 2.5-hour minimum at $200/hr actually comes to $500; no typical time range given; none of the estimate variables (stairs, drive time, walk distance, etc.) were explained.
Save Your Ass: prep speech never given — call ended before this stage.
Quote/Booking: no booking attempt, no deposit mention, no email handoff, no closing questions — call ended on the price objection.
Politeness: used 'Geraldine' only once (mostly 'ma'am'), short of the 3+ name-use bar; customer's mood declined and she hung up abruptly rather than ending positive.
Bonus: no rapport/humor moment, no insurance explanation, and no budget-conscious pivot offered once she said she couldn't afford $400 (e.g., smaller crew, adjusted scope).
top_strength: Arden proactively caught a detail most reps miss — he specifically flagged that the grandfather clock's internal weight and pendulum needed to be removed before the move, explaining why in plain terms: "our sensitive ma'am... the internal mechanical components including the weight and the pend has to be removed."
coaching_note: When Geraldine did the math out loud ($200 + $200 = $400), that was actually wrong — the 2.5-hour minimum at $200/hr is $500 — and Arden confirmed the wrong number instead of correcting it. That's a real accuracy problem with a budget-conscious customer. Once she said she couldn't afford it, that's the moment to slow down and problem-solve (smaller crew, adjusted scope) instead of apologizing and letting her go. Also build out the full pricing walk every time — no hidden fees, No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee — even on calls that feel like they're heading toward a no.
phone_presence_notes: Mostly scripted and disorganized (trailing sentences, repeated 'okay' filler, one question asked twice), no affirmations or rapport-building, and no acknowledgment when the customer got audibly frustrated at the end.
audio_review_reason: Score is low (2/Flat) and the ASR transcript is heavily garbled throughout — worth confirming actual tone matches the flat/disorganized read, especially in how the price objection was handled at the close.
